source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Identify the specific failed item(s) in the fire-safety check.
3. Record the exact location of the failure (e.g., "south stairwell smoke detector").
4. Describe the nature of the failure (e.g., "battery not present").
5. Note the date and time of the inspection.
6. Indicate any immediate corrective action taken, if applicable.
7. State whether a report to the local fire authorities is required or recommended.
8. Include notes on any potential hazards or risks identified due to the failed check.
9. Photograph or video any visual evidence if possible; ensure documentation includes date and time stamps.
10. Attach or reference any relevant drawings, schematics, or previous inspection reports for context.
11. Sign and date the report, indicating the identity and qualifications of the inspector.
12. Share the documented failure with building management or the responsible party promptly.
13. Recommend follow-up actions, including deadlines for corrections and re-testing
